title: Harmonia: A Unified Framework for Heterogeneous FPGA Acceleration in the Cloud
problem: The shell-role FPGA architecture adopted by cloud providers works well for homogeneous FPGA servers but fails to handle heterogeneous FPGA configurations: prior solutions either require laborious shell development for each FPGA variant (provider burden) or ad-hoc software modifications for each application (user burden), with no portable abstraction across diverse cloud FPGA types.
motivation: Cloud FPGA heterogeneity is growing rapidly as providers deploy different generations and families of FPGAs, but the shell-role split was designed for homogeneous deployments and does not scale to manage diverse hardware.
method: Harmonia introduces a standard interface (called a shell interface specification) that all FPGA types must follow, letting user accelerators be written once and work across different FPGA types without code changes. The framework defines platform-specific logic (the shell) according to this standard for each FPGA type on the hardware side. A software layer on top handles the differences between FPGA types automatically, so applications don't need custom code for each one.
key_novelty: A standardized interface specification and software abstraction layer that separate user accelerator code from FPGA-specific logic, allowing accelerators to be written once and deployed across different FPGA types.
contributions: Unified hardware shell interface specification enabling role portability across heterogeneous FPGAs
Software abstraction layer hiding FPGA-specific differences from user applications
Harmonia framework reducing provider shell development burden and user ad-hoc modification burden
limitations: Performance overhead of the unified abstraction layer not quantified in abstract; compatibility with proprietary cloud FPGA shells not discussed.
primary_theme: unified shell abstraction for heterogeneous cloud FPGA management
